chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min from Muawiya ibn Wahb said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any judge who rules between two parties and makes a mistake, he falls farther than the sky.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence for a judge who makes a mistake in ruling?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to underscore the immense spiritual weight of the Qadi’s role, where even a single error results in a fall 'farther than the sky.' This hyperbolic description highlights the severity of judicial negligence in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from mere civil liability. The hadith serves as a critical reminder for scholars and judges that their rulings carry eternal consequences, demanding rigorous adherence to both legal precision and moral integrity.
